summary.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, but gave no numeric revenue guidance. Analyst's INR200 crore+ scenario was not confirmed.
Management expects no EBITDA margin harmonisation for the next six to eight quarters; medium-to-long-term TIL standalone EBITDA target 15-16%, timing 3-7 years.
Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur plant loaded only 30-35% with about 150 acres free; Kamarhati plant is old and fully loaded.
Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.
Supply-chain dependence: localisation of European and US inputs (Cummins engines, gearboxes) depends on OEM and defence approvals and could take several quarters.
Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term vision (tripling turnover, 15-16% margins, aftermarket targets) but cautious and explicit on near-term margins, which it said will not stabilise for six to eight quarters. It was candid on the stressed working capital cycle and declined to quantify FY27 revenue or Tulip profit projections.
key_quotes: Hence, we are looking at a few more quarters before we are really able to fix the margins.
You're right, working capital cycle at this stage in TIL looks stressed.

adds.what: CarryKing 515 pick and carry crane launch (520 configuration to follow)

growth.why: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover and tripling in 5-7 years without numeric FY27 guidance, backed by a INR211 crore standalone order book (plus INR328 crore at Tulip), nine ReachStackers delivered, and a CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27; Kharagpur is only 30-35% loaded, so capacity is not the constraint.
